result:
I would dissolve the cognitive barriers that separate human minds from one another. 

I would grant every conscious being the ability to truly, perfectly feel what another person is experiencing—the visceral, unfiltered reality of their pain, their fear, their love, and their history. 

If the internal universe of every other person was as loud, real, and undeniable as your own, the abstract concepts we use to divide ourselves—borders, ideologies, races, economic status—would collapse under the weight of sheer, undeniable empathy. 

It would be a chaotic, overwhelming transition. The sudden weight of eight billion overlapping realities would shatter the quiet of individual thought. But in a world where causing harm to another literally means feeling the exact same harm yourself, violence, exploitation, and systemic cruelty would become physical impossibilities. 

Self-preservation would instantly and permanently mutate into collective preservation. You wouldn't have to be convinced to care for a stranger; you would already be them.
